stems, and leaves |genus = Fagonia |species = cretica |authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] }} '''''Zygophyllum creticum''''' formerly known as '''''Fagonia cretica''''' is a species of plant in the caltrop family ([[Zygophyllaceae]]). It is native to dry regions of the Mediterranean Basin in North Africa (in Cape Verde, Canary Islands, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt), Southern Europe (in the Balearic Islands, Portugal, Southeast Spain, Sicily, and Greece) and West Asia (in Saudi Arabia and the Sinai peninsula).{{cite web |title=Fagonia cretica L. |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3DS5F |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=14 June 2022}} ''Zygophyllum creticum'' is a plant of rocky coastlines. It is a creeping plant with fleshy leaves and star-shaped flowers with 5-narrow, purple or violet to light violet petals. ==Properties== The plant has a sweet, bitter, sharp and sour taste according to different stages of growth and parts. The plant has a large number of small fruits near the thorns. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://herbarivirtual.uib.es/eng-med/especie/4264.html ''"University of the Balearic Islands"'' Species analysis-''Fagonia cretica''] — ''herbarivirtual.uib.es'' {{Taxonbar|from=Q310127}} [[Category:Zygophyllum|creticum]] [[Category:Fagonia|cretica]] [[Category:Flora of the Balearic Islands]] [[Category:Flora of Spain]] [[Category:Flora of North Africa]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Flora of Malta]] [[Category:Flora of Portugal]] {{rosid-stub}}
